briefs.covers: Check 6 facade exception-handling fix (C1-C4), original freeze
SECURITY-PRIVACY-REVIEW.md F3, sanitizing str(exc) path leaks (C5 amendment). Brief marker updated to this ticket; DEVH-46 remains cited here.

requirement: Check 6 finding (dev-harness-33, independent): foreman_status_dashboard_data.py's load_atlas_snapshot() checks warehouse status once then makes 5 unhandled facade.fetch() calls, contradicting its own documented 'never silently as zero' promise.
done_state: load_atlas_snapshot() never crashes build_snapshot() when the warehouse's clean state flips between its initial status() check and a later facade.fetch() call, or when a raw sqlite3 error occurs mid-fetch; on either failure it returns a warehouse dict naming the real reason and tickets/gates data as None (never zero, never a silently-empty dict), and facade.close() is called on every exit path.

criteria.statement: A facade.fetch() call raising QueryRefused after the initial status() check reported clean does not crash build_snapshot(); it returns a warehouse dict naming the real reason and atlas_data of None.
criteria.verification: Construct a real ATLAS warehouse db, real-clean at the moment load_atlas_snapshot() calls facade.status(). Monkeypatch or otherwise force ONE of the five facade.fetch() calls to raise QueryRefused (simulating the warehouse's state flipping mid-script, e.g. a live ingest completing). Call build_snapshot() and assert it returns normally (no exception), the returned warehouse dict is not None and carries a field naming the QueryRefused reason, and every project's 'tickets'/'gates' values in the returned projects list are None, not 0 or {}.

criteria.statement: A raw sqlite3.Error raised mid-fetch (not just QueryRefused) is also caught, with the same behavior as C1.
criteria.verification: Same harness as C1, but the forced failure is a real sqlite3.Error (e.g. corrupt the warehouse db file between the status() check and a fetch call, or monkeypatch the connection to raise sqlite3.OperationalError). build_snapshot() must not crash; the same warehouse-dict-with-reason and None-not-zero behavior holds.

criteria.statement: facade.close() is called on every exit path from load_atlas_snapshot(), including when a fetch call raises -- not left leaked.
criteria.verification: In the C1/C2 forced-failure scenarios, assert the QueryFacade's underlying sqlite3 connection is genuinely closed after load_atlas_snapshot() returns (a further operation against that connection raises sqlite3.ProgrammingError, the documented behavior of a closed connection) -- not merely that a close() call appears in the source.

criteria.statement: The already-working paths are unaffected by this fix: construction-time QueryFacadeUnavailable, and the not-clean-at-first-status-check path, behave exactly as before.
criteria.verification: Re-run (or write, if none existed) a case for each: WAREHOUSE_DB pointing at a nonexistent/unmigrated file (QueryFacadeUnavailable at construction), and a warehouse whose status() is genuinely not clean at the first check (no fetch calls ever attempted). Both must return the same shape they did before this fix.

criteria.statement: Neither of load_atlas_snapshot()'s two exception-catch sites puts an exception's raw text (str(exc)) into the returned structure -- SECURITY-PRIVACY-REVIEW.md F3 (dev-harness-9b). QueryFacadeUnavailable's message embeds the warehouse's absolute filesystem path (observed directly: 'cannot open /Users/m5/dev/dev-harness-run2/atlas/warehouse/atlas.db read-only...'), and this module's own docstring promises outputs carry 'only the resolved prefix, not a human-readable name or path' -- the error paths must meet that same promise, not just the data paths C1's own docstring reference already covers.
criteria.verification: Force each of the two exceptions for real: (a) point WAREHOUSE_DB at a nonexistent/unmigrated file to trigger QueryFacadeUnavailable at construction; (b) monkeypatch facade.fetch() to raise QueryRefused or a real sqlite3.Error mid-fetch (the C1/C2 harness). In both cases, assert the absolute path string (or any substring of it, e.g. the warehouse filename or the repo root) never appears ANYWHERE in build_snapshot()'s returned structure -- serialize it with json.dumps(..., default=str) and grep the resulting text, not just the one field expected to carry it, since a raw exception could leak into more than one place. The reason field must still name something actionable: either the exception's TYPE (type(exc).__name__) or a fixed, hand-written sanitized string -- never str(exc) itself.

failure_criteria.statement: The except clause only catches QueryRefused, not sqlite3.Error, so a real database-level failure (a lock, a corrupt file, a schema change) still crashes build_snapshot() unhandled -- the fix looks complete because the one exception class that's easy to trigger in a quick test is covered, while the harder-to-trigger one that Check 6 also named is not.
failure_criteria.detection: C2 forces a real sqlite3.Error specifically, separate from C1's QueryRefused case.

failure_criteria.statement: facade.close() is moved into the except block only, not a finally, so the success path (no exception) never closes the connection -- inverts the original bug into a leak on the COMMON path instead of the rare one.
failure_criteria.detection: C3 checks close() actually happened by testing the connection's own closed state, and C4 confirms the non-exception paths still behave correctly.

failure_criteria.statement: tickets/gates default to an empty dict or 0 on the caught-exception path rather than None, so a consumer cannot tell 'the warehouse was queried and found nothing' from 'the query itself failed' -- the same class of ambiguity the module's own docstring already names as the thing to avoid ('never silently as zero').
failure_criteria.detection: C1 and C2 both assert None specifically, not falsy-in-general.

failure_criteria.statement: The fix redacts the reason field for one exception type but not the other, or only checks the one field the test author remembered rather than the whole serialized output -- a raw path could leak through a nested field, a log line folded into the structure, or a second copy of the reason.
failure_criteria.detection: C5 requires forcing BOTH exception types and grepping the whole json.dumps()'d structure for the path, not just the one field expected to carry it.
